title: India calls for Country-Driven Just Transition Mechanism at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye); Emphasizes Adequate Finance, Technology Transfer and Capacity Building for Developing Countries
subtitle:
Shri Bhupender Yadav calls for a Two-tier, Party-guided Mechanism that respects National Sovereignty and diverse National Circumstances
India stresses that Just Transition must address Employment, Social Protection, Adaptation, Poverty Eradication and Energy Access
body_text:
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today called for moving the global just transition agenda from dialogue and exchange of experiences towards practical, country-driven implementation. Addressing the Fourth Annual High-Level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition under the UAE Just Transition Work Programme at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye), the Minister reiterated India's commitment to an inclusive and equitable global transition that leaves no one behind. Presented India's views at the 4th Annual High-level Ministerial Roundtable on Just Transition on the sidelines of COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye today.

Underlined the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning.

India supports the operationalisation of a two-tier, Party-guided Mechanism, responsive to developing-country needs and respectful of national sovereignty and diverse national circumstances. — Bhupender Yadav (@byadavbjp) November 16, 2026 Shri Yadav emphasised that just transition must follow a whole-of-economy and whole-of-society approach, addressing employment, social protection, adaptation, poverty eradication, energy access and sustainable development. He highlighted that adequate financial support, technology transfer and capacity-building are essential to enable developing countries to implement their national priorities. Noting that there can be no one-size-fits-all approach, he cited India's sub-national heat action and disaster management plans, which address vulnerabilities of workers and communities, as well as the country's renewable energy expansion that seeks to combine low-carbon development with affordable energy access. These examples underline the need to integrate just transition considerations across adaptation, livelihoods and development planning, he added. The Minister underlined the need for clearly defined and complementary roles for the UAE Just Transition Work Programme and the proposed Just Transition Mechanism. While the Work Programme should continue to provide a platform for dialogue and exchange of experiences, the Mechanism should facilitate practical support through technical assistance, capacity-building and cooperation, translating the learnings from ongoing discussions into action, he stated. Reaffirming India's support for operationalising a two-tier, Party-guided Just Transition Mechanism, Shri Yadav stressed that it must be responsive to the needs of developing countries and respectful of national sovereignty and diverse national circumstances. The Mechanism should build on existing efforts, avoid duplication and facilitate access to adequate means of implementation. It must neither prescribe uniform sectoral pathways nor create new obligations, but enable countries to pursue their own just transition pathways in accordance with national priorities, while ensuring that workers, communities and vulnerable groups are not left behind, the Minister stressed. Shri Yadav observed that COP31 presents an important opportunity to move from exchanging experiences to practical, country-driven implementation. India stands ready to work constructively with all Parties towards an inclusive outcome that advances just transition while safeguarding the developmental priorities of developing countries, the Minister concluded. ***** VM
